explanation: COURSE-049 (Business Managemant) was retrieved (rank 1 of 15) and directly matches the respondent's own stated study_field_preference ('Commerce, business, or management'), yet the API's stated reason claims retrieved courses were 'primarily focused on language skills and technical training' -- an inaccurate summary of its own context. A plain sector/field-text match against this respondent's answers would have surfaced Business Managemant directly. RAG+LLM produced a worse outcome here than a naive baseline would have.

Correctly distinguished between two genuinely different ICT offerings within the same broad sector -- the general National Diploma in ICT and the specific Java Programming course -- both STRONG, both grounded in the respondent's own ideal_sector/study_field_preference answers. A sector-only filter would have returned the same or a larger undifferentiated list without this content-level distinction.

Correctly declined given genuinely weak evidence (ideal_sector and ideal_work_type both 'Not sure', study_field_preference 'Other field'). This is the correct behaviour and demonstrates the system does not force a recommendation from thin evidence -- but the value here is in correct restraint, not in richer reasoning, so it is not rated HIGH.

Same well-grounded ICT Diploma + Java Programming pair as respondent 3a86d117, here also connected to this respondent's stated barrier ('No suitable training available nearby') and training-type preference ('Professional/technical certification') -- a genuine multi-fact synthesis a sector filter could not produce.

COURSE-006 (ICT Diploma) and COURSE-073 (Java Programming) -- the same courses recommended for the other two ICT-interested respondents above -- were retrieved here too, and this respondent's stated obstacle ('work does not match my skills') plus ideal_sector ('Information technology and communications') plausibly support them. The API declined, reasoning that the courses don't support the stated 'start my own business' work-type preference. This is a defensible, non-fabricated distinction (technical training vs. entrepreneurship), so it is not scored NONE, but it looks more conservative than the identical-evidence case for 3a86d117/131a2b60, and arguably under-uses the sector+barrier match.

COURSE-012 (Refrigeration & AC Technician) was retrieved at rank 1 for a respondent whose ideal_sector is 'Manufacturing or production' with prior training and work-while-studying experience. The API declined because the courses didn't match 'work for a multinational company' specifically. Defensible as a literal reading, but skilled-trades/technical courses are a plausible, non-trivial link to a manufacturing-sector interest that went unused.

COURSE-008 (Computer Hardware Technician) and COURSE-029 (Mobile Phone Repair Technician) -- exactly the two courses the manual prototype recommended for this respondent -- were both retrieved (ranks 9-10 of 15) but not selected. The API's decline reasoning additionally cites the respondent's income_hours_preference ('fewer hours and less income') as a reason full-time courses 'may not be compatible' -- using a variable this project's own human-review audit flagged as describing CURRENT job hours preference, not course-schedule preference (a topic mismatch), as partial justification for a decline.

COURSE-019 (Quantity Surveying Assistant) and COURSE-023 (Construction Site Supervisor) -- exactly the two courses the manual prototype recommended -- were both retrieved (ranks 1 and 5 of 15) and directly match the respondent's stated ideal_sector ('Construction and building'). The API declined, incorrectly stating that retrieved courses were 'focused on business management, accounting, or other fields' that don't support construction interest -- again an inaccurate summary of its own context. It also added an unsupported eligibility claim ('educational background may not meet entry requirements... not explicitly stated but can be inferred') that the governance instructions explicitly prohibit (no eligibility claim without an explicit stated requirement). This is the clearest miss in the sample, on both matching and governance grounds.

Correctly declined given genuinely weak/unsure sector and work-type preferences, the correct behaviour for this deliberately weak-evidence test case. The reasoning also cites the respondent's 'current status as a student and primary household earner' as something that 'may limit their ability to commit' -- hedged with 'may', so not a hard rule-11 violation, but it leans on primary_earner_status in exactly the way this project's human-review audit flagged as a variable that should not independently justify a feasibility conclusion.

COURSE-007 (Professional Cookery), COURSE-011 (Baker) and COURSE-050 (Cake & Cake Structure) -- exactly the three courses the manual prototype recommended -- were all retrieved, directly matching the respondent's stated ideal_sector ('Hotels, restaurants, and hospitality'). COURSE-049 (Business Managemant) was also retrieved, plausibly supporting the respondent's 'start my own business' work-type preference. The API declined, reasoning that cookery/baking content doesn't 'directly support the specific entrepreneurial goals' -- a defensible-sounding but ultimately unconvincing rejection given both the sector match and the available business course were present in its own context and not combined.
